ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: It is known that the standard reaction enthalpy change of the reaction $\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}$ at 298 K is -801 kJ/mol. How many grams of methane are needed to react with excess oxygen to release 1500 kJ of heat?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the standard reaction enthalpy change of the reaction $\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}$ at 298 K is -801 kJ/mol. How many grams of methane are needed to react with excess oxygen to release 1500 kJ of heat?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the image is an average bond energy table, listing the average bond dissociation energies of C-H, O=O, C=O, and O-H; the bottom of the image gives the reaction equation CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(g), in which the stoichiometric coefficient of CH4 is 1. Reasoning: The problem statement gives that the standard reaction enthalpy change of this balanced combustion reaction is -801 kJ/mol, and the negative sign indicates heat release; since each occurrence of 1 mol of this reaction consumes 1 mol CH4, complete combustion of 1 mol CH4 releases 801 kJ of heat. To release 1500 kJ, the required amount of methane n = 1500/801 mol ≈ 1.873 mol. The molar mass of methane is 16 g/mol, so the mass m = n × 16 ≈ (1500/801) × 16 = 29.96 g, about 30 g.

raw_record.question_text: It is known that the standard reaction enthalpy change of the reaction $\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}$ at 298 K is -801 kJ/mol. How many grams of methane are needed to react with excess oxygen to release 1500 kJ of heat?

method.method_draft: From the text, take ΔH°rxn = -801 kJ/mol for the balanced combustion reaction. Since the image confirms the equation contains 1 mol CH4 per reaction event, 1 mol CH4 releases 801 kJ. Set n(CH4)=1500/801 mol, then convert to mass: m=n×16 g/mol ≈ (1500/801)×16 ≈ 29.96 g, which rounds to 30 g.
